goal: Realign three test files to the far-future expiry convention the rest of the suite already uses, and add a guard so the same time bomb cannot be planted again. Twelve enrollment-authority and capability tests began failing with 'enrollment capability must have a future expiry' between two suite runs that bracketed no relevant code change: green at 2026-08-19T17:46Z, red at 2026-08-20T01:12Z. The cause is not a regression in any slice. tests/kernel-enrollment-authority.test.ts, tests/kernel-p2b0-boundary.test.ts, and tests/kernel-canary-eligibility.test.ts hardcode expires_at as 2026-08-20T00:00:00.000Z at six sites, and that instant simply passed. Twenty-one other test files already express the same idea as 2099-01-01T00:00:00.000Z, so this is three files deviating from an established convention rather than a missing convention. A full scan of hardcoded ISO timestamps under tests/ found no other future-dated fixture, so these six sites are the complete set; the many 2026-08-12 and 2020-01-01 values are deliberately in the past to exercise expiry rejection and must not be touched. Replace the six sites with the far-future value, then add a guard that fails when any hardcoded absolute timestamp in tests/ is in the future but less than two years ahead. The guard must not flag deliberately past fixtures, and it is deliberately time-relative: a fixture written too close to the present starts failing about two years before it would silently expire, which converts a dormant time bomb into an early warning. This is the temporal form of the lesson recorded for the 2026-08-20-001 reconciliation: a test that hardcodes today's answer eventually drifts away from it, and hardcoding a future date guarantees it stops being future.

acceptance.assertion: The six expires_at sites across kernel-enrollment-authority, kernel-p2b0-boundary, and kernel-canary-eligibility no longer use a near-term date, and the twelve previously failing enrollment authority and capability tests pass.

A guard fails when a hardcoded absolute timestamp under tests/ is in the future but less than two years ahead, passes on the far-future convention, and does not flag the deliberately past fixtures such as 2026-08-12 and 2020-01-01 that exercise expiry rejection.
